h: Tips for a cracking climb in Oldham
p: Think of a session at Summit Up as a short, sharp burst of fun rather than an all-day affair. Allow a couple of hours in total once you've added travel, the safety talk and a drink afterwards. You'll want to arrive with a bit of time in hand, because harness fitting for a big group doesn't happen in thirty seconds, and nobody wants to lose climbing time to a queue.

A few things that make a real difference on the day. Eat something light beforehand, not a massive lunch. Keep nails short and take rings off, as they catch on holds. Bring a refillable bottle. And if someone in your group is nervous, let them watch a couple of climbers come down first, then start them on a low wall. Seeing how gently the auto-belay lowers people does wonders for the jitters.

There's normally a form to sign before anyone climbs, with a parent or guardian signing for under-18s, so check what's needed when you book and do it ahead if you can. Age guidance applies for little ones too.

Fancy fresh air afterwards? Alexandra Park in Oldham is a lovely Victorian park with a boating lake and plenty of room to run. Dovestone Reservoir, out in Saddleworth, is a favourite for an easy loop with big Pennine views, and the Metrolink tram links Oldham with Manchester city centre if you'd rather turn it into a city day.
